picks.description: Write an app once. It runs natively on the web, macOS, iOS, and Linux, and an AI agent can build it, run it, see it, and test it on every one of them.
picks.readmeHead:
# Exact **Write an app once. It runs natively on the web, macOS, iOS, and Linux, and an AI agent can build it, run it, see it, and test it on every one of them.** **Building an app?** With the tools installed ([Quick start, step 1](#1-install-the-tools)), run `bun scripts/exact.mjs setup` once, make the app with `bun scripts/exact.mjs new `, and read [`docs/start-here.md`](docs/start-here.md) (for a website, [`docs/start-here-site.md`](docs/start-here-site.md)): that guide is the only required reading. The rest of this page describes Exact for people deciding whether to use it or working on it. > [!TIP] > **Try it with a coding agent.** On a Mac with Xcode, Rust, Bun, and Chrome installed, > give Claude Code this prompt: > > ```text > Clone https://github.com/expo/exact and follow its README to make a new Exact > app with `exact new`. Run `bun scripts/exact.mjs setup` once first. Make a todo > list where I can add items, check them off, delete them, > and see how many are left. Put the view in Contract and keep the list in `app.ts`. > Write an `app.test.contract`, pass it on web, macOS, and the iOS Simulator with > `scripts/agent.mjs`, then open the app for me on all three. > ``` > > A fresh agent given the earlier version of this prompt on a clean clone (2026-10-04, Hermes already in the > machine cache, Cargo's cache warm) finished in about 57 minutes, and its tests passed > on all three platforms. About 25 of those minutes were the first macOS and iOS builds, > roughly 13 minutes each; later builds take a minute or two. On a machine that has > lacked Hermes, its source build came first and added time. Current setup downloads and > verifies the pinned host/iOS bundles once instead; ordinary builds stay offline.

picks.name: teardown
picks.description: A Claude Code skill that turns any machine into a 3D simulator you can take apart
picks.readmeHead:
# teardown

A Claude Code skill that turns any machine into a 3D simulator you can take apart.

Ask how something works. Claude builds it as one offline HTML page: the machine runs in the middle, every panel around it reads the real numbers, a button opens the part doing the work, and when nobody touches it the page tours itself.

![Mellis HB-7 robotic bee simulator](docs/bee.gif)

| Telson SC-8 robotic scorpion | Pelagos OC-8 robotic octopus |
|---|---|
| ![Telson SC-8 robotic scorpion](docs/scorpion.gif) | ![Pelagos OC-8 robotic octopus](docs/octopus.gif) |

## Install

```
npx skills add elvarofficial/teardown -g -a claude-code
```

Then, once, in the installed folder:

```
npm install && npx playwright install chromium
```

You need Node.js 20 or newer. For the video you also need `ffmpeg`, and for the sound Python 3.

## Use

Ask Claude Code in plain words:

> Build me a simulator of a 4-stroke motorcycle engine I can take apart.

> How does a mechanical watch keep time? Show me as a simulator.

> Make a teardown of a hydraulic excavator arm and record a 20-second video of it.

Or open one of the 3 examples first:

```
node sims/build.mjs v8-live          # teardown-out/dist/v8-live.html
node sims/build.mjs cessna-live
node sims/build.mjs strandbeest-live
```

## What is inside

| | |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md` | What Claude reads: how a machine is built, the rules that make it look right, the review loop. |
| `sims/kit/` | Runtime, stage, shader warm-up. |
| `sims/v8-*`, `sims/cessna-*`, `sims/strandbeest-*` | 3 complete machines. `-shared` is the machine, `-live` the page you drive, `-film` the recorded tour. |
| `sims/build.mjs` | Bundles a machine into one HTML file, three.js and fonts inlined. |
| `sims/capture.mjs` | Renders the film frame by frame to a 60 fps mp4, or to review sheets of stills. |
| `sfx/`, `run_sfx.py` | Procedural sound on the film's timeline, mastered to −14 LUFS. |

## Credits

Built on [whaleyxbt/claude-motion](https://github.com/whaleyx

picks.readmeHead: # NX2navi **Join the official NX2navi update discord server: https://discord.com/invite/uf6gSrsPpq** **NX2navi** is a static recompilation of *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time* for Nintendo Switch 2 (game version 1.1.1) into a native x86-64 application for Windows, with a Vulkan renderer ([docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)). > [!IMPORTANT] > **No game files are included.** You need your own legally obtained copy of the game, dumped from your own console. > Instructions for obtaining those files will not be provided. > > The game is built from your files on your machine, so the result contains the game. It is for your own use. Do not share it. ## Status Early development, playable. Kokiri Forest, Kakariko Village, Death Mountain Trail and its crater, the Temple of Time and the Great Fairy fountains play at 60 fps and above on current GPUs, from the title screen and from saves. Visual bugs and occasional crashes are still expected ([Known issues](#known-issues)). Report problems as issues, following [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Features - Native code, not emulation - 60 fps by default, or a limit of 30 to 240 fps, the display's refresh rate or unlimited - Native widescreen and ultrawide (the window's shape, 21:9 or 32:9) with the HUD, menus and movies kept 16:9 - Game resolutions from 1080p to above the game's 1440p: 1800p, 4K, 5K or the window's own size, sharp on high-DPI displays - Upscaling and anti-aliasing: NVIDIA DLSS (DLAA, Quality, Balanced, Performance, Ultra Performance; RTX GPUs) or AMD FSR 3.1 (Native AA and the same modes; any GPU) or AMD FSR 4 (the same modes; Radeon RX 6000, RX 7000 and RX 9000 GPUs), which render the 3D scene at the mode's share and keep the HUD sharp; or AMD FSR 1 or bilinear scaling to the window, with a sharpness setting; black bars or stretch - Frame generation: NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation (RTX 40 and 50 GPUs,
